source_title: Uttarakhand helicopter crash: Aircraft wreckage found, all 6 on board feared dead - The Times of India
source_excerpt: CHAMOLI: The wreckage of a helicopter that went missing in Uttarakhandâs Chamoli district has been found, and all six people on board, including the pilot, are dead, officials said.The aircraft was flying from Badrinath to Dehradun when it lost contact near Hathi Parvat (Hathi Pahad), close to Joshimath. Officials told PTI that the chopper crashed near Joshimath.Search operationFollowing the information of the missing chopper, the district administration launched an aerial search. According to PTI, two other helicopters were deployed to locate the aircraft.The district administration said the helicopter, operated by Trans Bharat Aviation, crashed into a hillside near the JP Power House, news agency PTI reported.Police, State Disaster Response Force (SDRF), Army and Indo-Tibetan Border Police (ITBP) personnel have been dispatched to the site for relief and rescue operations, officials said.In a post on X, chief minister Pushkar Singh Dhami said, "Reports have been received regarding an unfortunate helicopter crash near Chai village, close to Joshimath. A joint rescue operation is being conducted by the district administration, the Disaster Management Department, and the SDRF.â"I am personally monitoring the situation closely. I have issued instructions to ensure that those who are critically injured are immediately airlifted to a higher-level medical facility for better treatment. I pray to God for the safety of the passengers,â the post further read.Adverse weather in the regionThe incident comes amid adverse weather in Uttarakhand, with rain and snowfall reported in several parts of the state.Kedarnath Dham received the seasonâs first heavy snowfall after continuous snowfall since Thursday (October 29), with surrounding hills covered in snow and temperatures dropping sharply.Weather outlookDr CS Tomar, director of the Meteorological Centre, Dehradun, said rainfall activity is likely to continue over the next few days, particularly in hilly districts.He said heavy rainfall was recorded at eight to nine places on October 29, especially in Uttarkashi, Tehri and Haridwar districts.This is a developing story.(With agency inputs)Stay updated with the latest Dehradun news.
